note: doc/phase3_6_tasks_and_acceptance.md R36-BASE-02: every capability marked verified, limited or unimplemented, with the evidence for each. Section 2 also requires what this integration actually supports to be listed separately from what R2 left undone, and forbids the handoff baseline from depending on the latter.

R3_5.why: The pinned Triton wheel does not export AxisInfo. Two routes were tried and recorded: the Python API has no such symbol, and upstream's TTIR to TTGIR conversion leaves sizePerThread at 1 whether an access is contiguous or stride-7, so its conclusion is not observable in the layout either. The route that remains is a separate tool built against Triton's own pinned LLVM.
R3_5.bearing_on_this_stage: None of R3.6's thirty standards depends on AxisInfo. The contract's precondition is not fully met and that is recorded here rather than assumed away; the compiler this stage integrates is the one that was measured, and its gains were verified independently.

capabilities.what: a @triton.jit kernel through the real Triton frontend to TNCA machine code
capabilities.limits: one element per lane; a wider block is refused rather than lowered

capabilities.what: a TNCA IR program through the product builder
upstream canonicalisation and CSE, constant and compare lowering, dead pure and unobservable-other elimination, LinearLayout-driven view elision
capabilities.limits: no reordering is attempted; no AxisInfo facts are used or claimed

capabilities.what: a versioned artifact with its manifest, ABI and identity
session, buffer, event, launch, wait, drain against the simulated device
a grid of programs over one core, run sequentially
capabilities.limits: grid=2 runs sequentially on one core. It is NOT a claim about two tiles; R3 v2 says so in the inventory.

capabilities.what: four tiles with the mesh and system runtime
capabilities.evidence: make e2e (2 tests), make core4, make top
capabilities.limits: the RTL and a four-block grid run; the SYSTEM runtime that R2 specified is not complete. R2-09, R2-10 and R2-14 have open halves. Nothing in this stage's handoff baseline depends on it.

capabilities.what: a banked, finite-port vector register file with real arbitration
capabilities.evidence: R3 v2, all eight gates; spec/r3v2_contract.json
capabilities.limits: one read and one write accepted per bank per cycle, four banks, 8 KiB

capabilities.what: the accumulator file with the same treatment as the VRF
capabilities.evidence: R3V2-SYN-01 states it explicitly: the ARF is 16 KiB and is NOT counted toward the synchronous-memory ratio, and is still behavioural
capabilities.limits: 16 KiB, behavioural. R3.6 does not undertake it and must not report it as done or guarantee it maps to an FPGA RAM. Section 4.4 says so in as many words.

capabilities.what: coherence between host and device views, or system atomics
capabilities.limits: host and device access is serial and the runtime enforces it. Section 4.5 permits that and forbids claiming what is not there.

capabilities.what: an execution backend other than the built-in simulator binding
capabilities.evidence: none yet; R36-BE-02 is what would change this
capabilities.limits: the runtime currently starts and speaks to one simulator directly

capabilities.what: a self-contained hardware package that elaborates outside this repository
capabilities.evidence: none yet; R36-RTL-01 is what would change this
capabilities.limits: the RTL runs only from inside this repository today: the benches load programs with $readmemh and the source list is the Makefile's. Section 4.3 wants a package with its own top, ports and dependency closure, and section 4.3 also forbids the shared hardware's only control path being a simulator facility.

capabilities.what: a bitstream, a board, or a process mapping
capabilities.limits: Section 1 puts device selection, vendor IP, pin and board constraints, place and route, bitstream, programming and on-board debug in a separate branch. Not a failure of this stage.

r2_remaining.note: Section 2: what this integration supports and what R2 left undone are listed apart, and the handoff baseline may not depend on the latter.
open: R2-09 and R2-10 four-tile device halves
